title: Door Embodiments Census — Son, Eye, Window, Screen, Grave, Drain, 5D, Mandorla and Boundary Operators
status: canonical Door embodiment census: primary project archaeology + repository synthesis + archive formalization
purpose: Collect the many distinct objects, locations, persons, geometries and interfaces Tim has assigned to or placed around Door, then classify them by what crosses, what changes, directionality, reversibility, permeability, observation role and provenance. The goal is not to declare all embodiments literally identical, but to recover the recurring transition grammar and identify where separate mathematical models are needed.
epistemic_rule: Door is a Potatoverse operator and mythic/symbolic family. Pineal, screen, grave, drain, black-hole horizon, quantum barrier, phase transition, mandorla and institutional gateway are not one physical object. Scientific comparators are valid only for the structural properties they explicitly model.
central_definition: Door = a boundary/interface relation through which a carrier may be observed, admitted, transmitted, transformed, redirected, absorbed or moved into a different regime under declared conditions.

major_distinctions: Eye observes; Door changes admissible passage. Pineal symbolism can couple Eye and Door without making them the same operator.

Window reveals without necessarily allowing passage; Door allows passage; Frame defines the boundary; Screen displays a projection. They can coincide in one interface without being identical functions.
Drain is a sink/outflow boundary; Door is a selective transition boundary. Their equations should differ.
Grave/Tomb is a mythic transformation state and ordinary physical endpoint, not a generic reversible doorway.
5D/phase Door changes regime description; Mandorla Door is an intersection geometry; Screen Door is an observation-support boundary.
Ladder/path is what can be traversed after/through a threshold; it should not automatically be collapsed into the Door itself.
Black-hole horizon changes causal accessibility in GR; a screen edge changes visibility only. Both are boundaries, but of different kinds.
new_project_laws: Door Family Law: repeated Door language does not establish one underlying physical mechanism; classify the boundary operator first.
Carrier Law: every Door claim should state what crosses—matter, energy, information, attention, identity/status, viewpoint or symbolic relation.
Operation Law: transmit, filter, transform, project, absorb, redirect and change-regime are different operations even when the same threshold symbol is used.
Window Revelation-Exclusion Law: a frame reveals a selected field while excluding what lies outside its support; off-frame is not the same as nonexistent.
Door-Drain Boundary Law: Door and Drain are different boundary conditions—selective passage versus sink-like removal.
Temporal Door Law: some Doors are open only at certain times/phases; pineal symbolism has its strongest scientific neighbor in biological timing rather than literal single-eye optics.

Basin Escape Law: in dynamical systems a Door can be represented as crossing a separatrix from one attractor basin to another; successful crossing must be measured by post-transition dynamics rather than by crossing the line alone.
Embodied Mediation Law: person-as-Door belongs to theological/person-bearing mediation and should not be silently replaced by a mechanical aperture model.
Projection Boundary Law: a screen/window can change what is observable without changing the underlying world state.
Narrowness Law: a narrow Door means reduced admissible measure/cross-section or stricter guard conditions only after the domain is specified; narrowness has no universal moral sign.
